keys: Clinical diagnosis with empiric medical therapy (NSAIDs, CHCs, progestins, GnRH agonists/antagonists, elagolix). TVUS first imaging (deep infiltrating disease). Laparoscopy not required for diagnosis. Avoid biomarker testing.

name: ACOG Gestational Diabetes 2024 (CPG #2)
keys: Universal 2-step screen at 24-28 wk: 50g GCT → 100g 3h OGTT if abnormal; Carpenter-Coustan criteria (2 of 4 abnormal). Early screening if BMI ≥25 (≥23 Asian) + risk factors (A1c ≥5.7, prior GDM, PCOS). Lifestyle first; insulin preferred if pharmacologic needed (metformin/glyburide cross placenta, second-line). Targets: fasting <95, 1h pp <140, 2h pp <120. Delivery 39-40w (A1), 39w (A2 controlled). Postpartum 75g OGTT 4-12 wk; 50-70% lifetime T2DM risk.

name: NAMS 2020 Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause Position Statement
keys: Non-hormonal lubricants/long-acting moisturizers first for mild symptoms. Low-dose vaginal estrogen (cream, tablet, ring) first-line prescription for moderate-severe GSM; minimal systemic absorption, endometrial protection generally not required. Vaginal DHEA (prasterone) and oral ospemifene (SERM) effective alternatives. Systemic ET if vasomotor symptoms coexist. Energy-based therapies (CO2 laser, RF) insufficient evidence; not recommended outside trials.

name: PCOS - 2023 International Evidence-Based Guideline (ACOG PB 194 is 2018, reaffirmed 2025)
keys: CITATION FIX: there is NO ACOG PCOS Practice Bulletin dated 2022. ACOG Practice Bulletin 194 is dated 2018 (reaffirmed 2025). The current international standard is the 2023 International Evidence-Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of PCOS (Monash/ESHRE/ASRM, Aug 2023; endorsed by 39 organizations). DIAGNOSTIC CHANGE: serum AMH can now SUBSTITUTE for pelvic ultrasound in establishing polycystic ovarian morphology in ADULTS (other etiologies excluded) - ultrasound is no longer required. Rotterdam 2-of-3 otherwise retained (oligo/anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, polycystic morphology); exclude thyroid disease, hyperprolactinemia, and nonclassic CAH. Management: lifestyle first-line; combined OCP for menstrual irregularity and hyperandrogenism; metformin for metabolic features; letrozole first-line for ovulation induction (over clomiphene). Screen for metabolic syndrome, OSA, depression, and endometrial hyperplasia.

name: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy PPP 2024
keys: Annual dilated exams: T1DM start 5y after onset; T2DM at diagnosis. Anti-VEGF (aflibercept, ranibizumab, bevacizumab, faricimab) first-line for center-involved DME. PRP for proliferative DR. Tighter glycemic + BP control slow progression (DCCT, UKPDS).

name: AAO Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma 2025
keys: Latanoprost or other PG analog first-line (UKGTS: -3.8 mmHg, slows VF progression). Add second/third agents to reach target IOP 25-30% reduction. SLT (selective laser trabeculoplasty) per LiGHT trial - first-line alternative. MIGS for moderate disease.

name: AAO Age-Related Macular Degeneration 2024
keys: Wet AMD: anti-VEGF (aflibercept, faricimab, ranibizumab, brolucizumab) monthly initially, then treat-and-extend or PRN. Dry AMD: AREDS2 (lutein/zeaxanthin/zinc/Cu/vit C/E) slows progression 25% (no benefit if smoker for AREDS). Geographic atrophy: pegcetacoplan/avacincaptad pegol new.

name: GCA vision loss (teaching lens on ACR/VF 2021 - not a separate guideline)
keys: ATTRIBUTION FIX: there is NO joint ACR/EULAR GCA 2021 management guideline. ACR and EULAR jointly published 2022 ACR/EULAR CLASSIFICATION CRITERIA for GCA (a classification instrument, not a management guideline). This entry is a vision-loss teaching lens on the ACR/VF 2021 guideline - do not cite it as a separate society document. OPHTHALMIC EMERGENCY: GCA is the leading cause of preventable sudden bilateral blindness in older adults. Start HIGH-DOSE GLUCOCORTICOIDS IMMEDIATELY on clinical suspicion - do NOT wait for biopsy or for ESR/CRP. IV pulse methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3 days if any visual symptoms (amaurosis fugax, diplopia, vision loss); once vision is lost it rarely recovers, and the fellow eye is at high risk within days. Arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy: pallid disc swelling. Check ESR AND CRP (either may be normal); platelets often elevated. Temporal artery biopsy within 2 weeks of starting steroids (yield persists); ultrasound halo sign is an alternative. Tocilizumab steroid-sparing; upadacitinib FDA-approved for GCA April 2025.

name: AAN/AAO Optic Neuritis (ONTT)
keys: ONTT: IV methylprednisolone 1g/d x 3d + oral pred speeds visual recovery (~2 wks vs ~5 wks placebo). Oral pred ALONE inferior - increases recurrence. No long-term VA benefit. MRI predicts MS conversion (15-yr: 50% if abnormal vs 22% if normal).

name: AAO-HNS Acute Rhinosinusitis 2025
keys: Watchful waiting OR amoxicillin-clavulanate 5-7d for uncomplicated ABRS. Watchful waiting if reliable follow-up. Antibiotic if symptoms >=10d or worsening or severe (T>39, facial pain). Imaging only if complications (orbital/intracranial).

name: AAP/AAFP Acute Otitis Media 2013
keys: Diagnose with TM bulging or fluid + recent symptoms. Severe: T>=39 or moderate-severe otalgia or >=48h symptoms = antibiotics. Mild + reliable follow-up = watchful waiting. Amoxicillin 80-90 mg/kg/day; amoxicillin-clavulanate if treatment failure / recent ATB.

name: IDSA Group A Strep Pharyngitis 2025 (Part 1: testing) + 2012 (treatment)
keys: TESTING - 2025 Part 1 (Oct 2025) CHANGES PRACTICE: clinical scoring systems (Centor/McIsaac, FeverPAIN) now explicitly gate WHETHER TO TEST AT ALL - do NOT test and do not treat low-risk patients. This reverses the 2012 posture of near-universal RADT or culture in adults with pharyngitis. TREATMENT - Part 2 (treatment, duration, penicillin allergy) is still PENDING (estimated late 2026), so 2012 treatment guidance still stands: penicillin V or amoxicillin first-line for 10 days; cephalosporin, clindamycin, or azithromycin if penicillin-allergic; no test of cure after RADT in adults.

name: AAO-HNS Sudden SNHL 2019
keys: Idiopathic SNHL: high-dose oral steroids within 2 weeks (prednisone 1 mg/kg x 7-14d). Intratympanic dexamethasone if oral failure / contraindication. Hyperbaric O2 + steroids for salvage <1 mo. MRI to rule out vestibular schwannoma.

name: AAO-HNS Hoarseness 2018
keys: Laryngoscopy if dysphonia >4 weeks or earlier with red flags (smoker, hemoptysis, neck mass, dysphagia). Avoid empiric PPI for non-LPR symptoms. Voice therapy for muscle tension dysphonia.

name: AHRQ Quality Indicators (PSI/IQI/PQI)
keys: Patient Safety Indicators (PSI): hospital-acquired adverse events. Inpatient Quality Indicators (IQI): mortality, utilization. Prevention Quality Indicators (PQI): ambulatory-care-sensitive admissions. Used for hospital comparison and CMS pay-for-performance.

name: IHI Quintuple Aim 2022
keys: The QUINTUPLE AIM is IHI current and supersedes the Triple Aim for teaching. Evolution: TRIPLE Aim (IHI 2008 - improve population health, improve patient experience, reduce per-capita cost) -> QUADRUPLE Aim (Bodenheimer and Sinsky 2014 - adds clinician well-being) -> QUINTUPLE Aim (Nundy, Cooper, Mate; IHI/JAMA 2022 - adds HEALTH EQUITY). Presenting the Triple Aim as IHI current framework is out of date.

name: IHI Model for Improvement (PDSA)
keys: Three questions: aim? measures? changes? PDSA cycles (Plan-Do-Study-Act) for iterative testing. Run charts and SPC for measurement. Integrated with Lean / Six Sigma DMAIC.

name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics 2024
keys: Four principles: autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice. Capacity (clinical, decision-specific, can fluctuate) vs competence (legal, global). Informed consent: information + voluntariness + capacity. No ethical difference between withholding/withdrawing care.

name: USPSTF Methodology + Grade Definitions
keys: Grade A (high certainty, substantial benefit): offer/provide. Grade B (moderate benefit): offer. Grade C (small benefit): selectively offer. Grade D (no benefit/harm): don't offer. Grade I (insufficient): document limitations.

name: IDSA/SHEA Antimicrobial Stewardship
keys: Core elements: leadership commitment, accountability, drug expertise. Strategies: preauthorization, prospective audit + feedback, formulary restriction. Reduces CDI 26%, costs ~$200-400K/yr/hospital. CDC Core Elements mandated by Joint Commission.

name: USPSTF Recommendations 2024
keys: A/B grade: cancer screening (mammography 40-74, colonoscopy/FIT 45-75, lung LDCT 50-80, cervical HPV 30-65). HTN screening adults. Statin 40-75 with ASCVD risk >=10%. Aspirin 40-59 with ASCVD risk >=10% individualized. AAA screening 65-75 male smokers.

name: ACIP Adult Immunizations 2025
keys: Influenza annually, COVID-19. Tdap once + Td q10y. RZV >=50, RSV >=75 (60-74 risk-based), pneumococcal PCV21/PCV20/PCV15 >=50, HPV through 45. MMR/varicella if no immunity. Travel: hepatitis A/B, typhoid, yellow fever.

name: ACC/AHA ASCVD Risk Calculator (PREVENT 2025)
keys: PREVENT replaces pooled cohort equations: more accurate across race/ethnicity. Includes kidney function (eGFR), glycemia, social determinants. 10-year + 30-year ASCVD risk. Statin shared decision >=7.5% 10-year risk.

name: USPSTF Aspirin for Primary CV Prevention 2022
keys: Initiate ASA 81 mg in 40-59 with 10-yr ASCVD risk >=10% (C grade - small benefit). Do NOT initiate >=60 (D grade - bleeding outweighs). ARRIVE/ASCEND/ASPREE shifted recommendations away from broad primary prevention.

name: USPSTF Tobacco Cessation 2021 + ATS 2020 Pharmacotherapy
keys: 5As (Ask, Advise, Assess, Assist, Arrange) all adults (A grade). Combination behavioral + pharmacotherapy most effective. ATS 2020: varenicline (nicotinic partial agonist) > NRT > bupropion (EAGLES showed no excess neuropsychiatric/CV events). Varenicline + nicotine patch superior to monotherapy. Extended duration (12→24 wk) increases abstinence. Pregnancy: behavioral only (insufficient evidence for pharmacotherapy). E-cigarettes: insufficient evidence (I statement); not first-line.

name: AAHPM Pain Management 2024
keys: Multimodal: WHO ladder (NSAIDs/acetaminophen -> weak opioids -> strong opioids). Methadone unique (NMDA antagonist + mu agonist - QT, drug interactions). Adjuvants: gabapentinoids (neuropathic), dexamethasone (bone), bisphosphonates. Opioid rotation if dose-limiting toxicity.

name: AAHPM Goals-of-Care 2024 (EPAs)
keys: Ask-tell-ask framework. Elicit values, not just preferences. Document POLST/MOLST across settings. Five wishes / advance directive components: medical decisions, person to make them, comfort, treatment, family. Code status discussion before procedures.

name: ASCO Palliative Care for Patients With Cancer 2024
keys: 2024 update REPLACES 2017. Core recommendation unchanged: refer to interdisciplinary palliative care EARLY and CONCURRENTLY with cancer therapy from diagnosis of advanced disease (TEMEL: improved QoL, mood, possibly survival). NEW IN 2024: early integration explicitly EXTENDED to patients with HEMATOLOGIC MALIGNANCIES and to patients enrolled on EARLY-PHASE CLINICAL TRIALS - both under-addressed in 2017. Explicit endorsement of TELEHEALTH-delivered palliative care, and of needs-based prioritization plus primary palliative care by the oncology team to manage capacity constraints. Hospice eligibility: prognosis of 6 months or less. Hospital-based palliative care reduces ICU days and costs.
